A01.name: Broken Access Control
A01.guidance: Deny by default, enforce access control server-side on every request, disable directory listing, and log access-control failures.

A02.name: Cryptographic Failures
A02.guidance: Serve all traffic over TLS, enable HSTS, mark cookies Secure, and use current algorithms and key lengths.

A03.name: Injection
A03.guidance: Use parameterised queries and safe APIs, validate input server-side with allow-lists, and contextually encode output.

A04.name: Insecure Design
A04.guidance: Apply threat modelling and secure design patterns; do not rely on client-side controls.

A05.name: Security Misconfiguration
A05.guidance: Use a hardened, repeatable configuration: send security headers, remove version banners and unused features/services, and review CORS policies.

A06.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
A06.guidance: Inventory components and versions, remove unused dependencies, and patch from official sources promptly.

A07.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
A07.guidance: Use MFA where possible, strong session management, rate limiting, and no default or hard-coded credentials.

A08.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
A08.guidance: Verify integrity of code and data (signatures, SRI), and avoid deserialising untrusted data.

A09.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
A09.guidance: Log security-relevant events with enough context, protect logs from injection, and alert on suspicious activity.

A10.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
A10.guidance: Validate and allow-list destination URLs server-side, and block requests to internal address ranges.

rules.basis: Project rule: a missing HTTP security header is a hardening/configuration gap (A05).
Project rule: software/version banners are default-configuration information leaks (A05).
Project rule: a session cookie sent without the Secure flag can travel in cleartext (A02, CWE-614).
Project rule: missing cookie hardening attributes are configuration issues (A05).
Project rule: content served without TLS exposes data in transit (A02, CWE-319).
Project rule: permissive CORS policy is a misconfiguration (A05, CWE-942).
Project rule: directory listing exposes files without authorization (A01, CWE-548).
Potential mapping: an exposed service may be unnecessary (A05). Manual review is needed to confirm.
